changelog: Replaced C3 to explicitly penalize cuts that strand predicates or obligatory complements/scope-bearing elements, addressing the primary finding that head–complement splits are treated too crudely.

Replace C3 to directly address the primary finding: make the rule explicitly penalize cuts that strand predicates, required complements, or scope-bearing operators (per the diagnosis and its example evidence).
Delete E7 because it is one of the largest example units and removing it reclaims prompt space (size_feedback required net shortening).
Delete E3 because it is large and hand-crafted; removing it reduces total chars to meet the budget.
Delete E5 because it is large and hand-crafted; removing it further ensures the prompt falls under the character budget.
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_1507 to teach head–complement / relative-clause splits (addresses primary finding about stranded complements).
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_1280 to illustrate prepositional-complement and object attachment risks (predicate-argument cohesion).
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_1285 to show negation/scope-bearing operator risks (cuts that flip meaning if stranded).
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_1543 to demonstrate complement-clause ('where' clause) attachments and their cohesion impact.

Replace C7 to explicitly demote cuts that separate scope-bearing operators (negation, modals, auxiliaries, quantifiers, complementizers) from their arguments or complements when the pre-cut span would assert a claim — addresses the primary finding about stranded predicates/obligatory complements causing contradictions.
